stem: A Valium prescription with unused refills was issued seven months ago. Which federal deadline controls?

choices.text: Dispense because unused refills remain valid for one year.
Use the date of the last refill to start a new six-month period.
Renew the prescription based solely on the patient's request.
The prescription is no longer refillable six months after issue.
Transfer it and apply a new issue date at the receiving pharmacy.

explanation.core_reasoning: The prescription is no longer refillable six months after issue. By contrast, 'Dispense because unused refills remain valid for one year.' uses a legal trigger absent from the stem.

choice_analysis.A: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Dispense because unused refills remain valid for one year.
choice_analysis.B: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Use the date of the last refill to start a new six-month period.
choice_analysis.C: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Renew the prescription based solely on the patient's request.
choice_analysis.D: The stated facts support this result: The prescription is no longer refillable six months after issue.
choice_analysis.E: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Transfer it and apply a new issue date at the receiving pharmacy.

related_facts: diazepam (Valium) is used for anxiety disorders, acute alcohol withdrawal, muscle spasm, and adjunctive seizure treatment; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
explanation.mpje_trap: Reject 'Dispense because unused refills remain valid for one year.' because its legal trigger is absent.
